name: Multi-Vari Chart
description: Stages single measurements across up to four factors and splits the spread into variance components — shows where the variation actually comes from.
whenToUse: When the spread of a measured characteristic must be traced to its sources: stages every single measurement by two to four factors (for example shift, cavity, part) and splits the variance into components, nested or crossed, by ANOVA or REML; needs one numeric measurement column and two factor columns.
factorsHint: The order drives layout and nesting alike — drag to reorder.
interpretation: {term} contributes the largest share of the total variation at {percent} %.
interpretationError: Repeat variation is the largest share at {percent} % — the chosen factors barely explain the spread.
unbalancedNote: Unbalanced design: the variance components depend on the estimator here. REML is the more dependable choice in this case.
clampedNote: Negative variance estimates were clamped to 0 — a sign of too little data for the finest level.
warn_unbalanced: Unbalanced design — not every factor combination is equally occupied.
warn_noReplicates: No replicates — the finest source has a single observation per cell and was pooled into the residual error.
warn_rowCapExceeded: Too many rows for the REML estimate — the calculation fell back to the ANOVA method.
warn_notConverged: The REML estimate did not converge — the variance components are approximations.
warn_negativeComponent: A negative variance estimate was set to zero — this source is not distinguishable from zero.
warn_aliasedTerms: At least one component is not estimable in this design (0 degrees of freedom) and was removed before the REML fit — the reported value of 0 is not an estimate, it is aliasing.
warn_emptyCells: Empty cells — at least one factor combination does not occur in the data.
warn_tooManyAxisLevels: “{col}” has {count} levels on the x axis (limit: {max}) — the chart is therefore not drawn. Put a factor with fewer levels in position 1.
warn_tooManySeriesLevels: “{col}” has {count} series levels (limit: {max}) — the chart is therefore not drawn. Put a factor with fewer levels in position 2.
warn_tooManyPanels: “{col}” produces {count} panels (limit: {max}) — the chart is therefore not drawn. The variance-components table below remains valid.
warnDroppedRows: {count} row(s) skipped: empty factor level or non-numeric measurement.
errNoData: No usable measurements in the selected columns.
errCompute: Variance components could not be computed: {msg}

invariants.factorIds: Every factor row needs its own, non-empty id.
invariants.factorCount: There must be at least two and at most four factor rows.
